title: Humpty Dumpty burns former Hatfield Chips 1981
description: In 1968, F. H. Hatfield, President of Hatfield Industries Limited in Hartland, N.B., and N. Kishfy, Managing Director of Humpty Dumpty Potato Chip Company in Lachine, Quebec, jointly announced that Hatfield Industries Limited had become an affiliate of Humpty Dumpty. Mr. Hatfield subsequently assumed the role of Chairman of the Board. As seen in the photo, the Humpty Dumpty sign is twisted because a fire broke out at around 3:30 a.m. on October 6, 1981, as recounted by employee Dana Clark, who was working that night. “The fryer had been shut down during the day for maintenance, which allowed us to catch up on cleaning and painting. While we were taking our lunch break in the dining room, Dale Hayes walked in and calmly told Stillman Tibbits he’d better come: ‘I think she’s all afire.’ With no cell phones, someone had to drive to the fire hall to push the button to sound the long, continuous blast. Years of accumulated chip grease fueled the blaze, turning the building into a red-hot inferno, and everyone could only watch in disbelief."
